item: Integration `deletionPolicy: Delete` lifecycle (tracker F09b "Delete needs a cleanup/finalizer protocol", F60c "Delete lifecycle ... still open")
summary: The previous agent's report is accurate but understated: on SQLite a `Delete`-policy Integration never runs at all, and on Kubernetes no Integration runs at all. The field is declared at /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru/api/v1alpha1/integration_types.go:232-236 (enum Retain;Delete, default Retain), mirrored in three CRD copies (deploy/kustomize/crd/bases/kudurru.io_integrations.yaml:191-198, deploy/helm/kudurru-crds/templates/kudurru.io_integrations.yaml:192, internal/store/validator/crds/kudurru.io_integrations.yaml:191) and re-checked by the host at ee/integration/host/input.go:201. The SQLite root adapter refuses any instance with `Delete` before provider work (cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go:292-296, returns ErrUnsupported), which surfaces only as an opaque `Degraded/ProvisionFailed` (ee/integration/host/commands.go:110-142); cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime_test.go:345-387 asserts zero polls and zero budget rows. With `Retain`, deleting the object is a plain store delete (no code ever sets a finalizer on an Integration): the host cancels and joins the job and forgets its status (ee/integration/host/lifecycle.go:111-118, 160-165), live inventory/MAC claims are withdrawn from the next image (cmd/kudurru/integration_image.go:101-103; test integration_runtime_test.go:172-183), but source-owned DNSRecordSets, IntegrationSourceHead/Chunk/NameAllocation rows, IntegrationLedger/Operation rows and Cloudflare records all stay (no non-test code deletes a ledger or operation row; the only readers are ee/integration/host/engine.go:292 and ee/integration/ledger/repository.go:23,38). On Kubernetes the host is not mounted (cmd/kudurru/serve.go:1083-1084), so either policy is inert there. Most building blocks for a cleanup protocol already exist: both store drivers honor finalizers/deletionTimestamp (internal/store/sqlite/crud.go:581-583, 603-666; internal/store/sqlite/command.go:392-414; internal/store/kube/crud.go:267-273), the planner already emits owned-only deletes ordered first (ee/integration/plan/diff.go:142-148, 218-221, 303-316), the Cloudflare adapter already executes and receipts delete intents with a remote reread (ee/integration/cloudflare/apply.go:54-87, 255-259, 292-297), recovery already confirms observed absence (ee/integration/host/engine.go:518-531), and every HTTP attempt is budgeted (ee/integration/host/request.go:49-86). What is missing is the terminating job mode, a ledger "forget" transition, the atomic local purge, finalizer arming/removal, store hardening so a manager's whole-object Apply cannot strip the cleanup finalizer (sqlite crud.go:516-558 takes finalizers from the caller's document; kube Force takeover crud.go:158-160), plus status/CLI/docs. No owner blocker exists for the SQLite work; the Kubernetes half depends on the separate Kubernetes host mount.
alreadyDone: Nothing the tracker lists as open for this item is secretly finished: `Delete` is genuinely unimplemented. The entries below are prerequisites that already exist and should be reused, not rebuilt.

Schema/validation of the field on both carriers: api/v1alpha1/integration_types.go:232-236; CRD enum+default at deploy/kustomize/crd/bases/kudurru.io_integrations.yaml:191-198; validator rejects unknown values and defaults to Retain (internal/store/validator/integration_test.go:34, 60); host re-validates (ee/integration/host/input.go:201); generated reference docs-site/content/reference/crds/integration.md:63.

Fail-closed refusal instead of silently treating Delete as Retain (the alternative rejected in D239, dev-docs/design-record.md:1839): cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go:292-296, tested by TestIntegrationRuntimeRefusesDeleteAndUnlicensedExecution (cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime_test.go:345-387); documented at docs/deploy/integrations.md:14-15 and docs/architecture/integrations.md:155-161.

Retain semantics on SQLite are implemented, tested and documented: job cancel/join and status forget (ee/integration/host/lifecycle.go:111-118, 160-165); live claims withdrawn when the same-UID Integration is absent or deleting (cmd/kudurru/integration_image.go:101-103); TestIntegrationRuntimeActualSourceCommitAndWithdrawal deletes the object and proves withdrawal without a replayed poll (integration_runtime_test.go:172-183); docs/deploy/integrations.md:128-131, 140.

Durable terminating state is native in both stores: SQLite Delete on an object with finalizers sets deletionTimestamp in the delete transaction and the Apply clearing the last finalizer removes it (internal/store/sqlite/crud.go:581-583, 603-666; transaction-bound variant command.go:392-414; tests internal/store/sqlite/sqlite_test.go:458 TestFinalizers and cmd/kudurru/serving_object_sources_test.go:431-490 for file-source deletion); Kubernetes relies on the apiserver (internal/store/kube/crud.go:267-273; internal/store/kube/crud_test.go:319 TestDeleteHonoursFinalizers).

The host and root already treat a set deletionTimestamp as a distinct state: host pauses with reason `Deleting` (ee/integration/host/lifecycle.go:111, 170-181); every normal fence refuses it (cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go:366, 450); the lifecycle comment explicitly reserves cleanup for root admission (lifecycle.go:160).

Ownership proof and delete planning: remote marker = digest(clusterID, UID) in the Cloudflare comment (ee/integration/cloudflare/ownership.go:14-38); planner counts a row as owned only by marker or by ledger ProviderIDs evidence for legacy cluster-only markers, never deletes foreign/unowned rows, and blocks conflicted names (ee/integration/plan/diff.go:142-148, 183-186, 218-221); deletes ordered before updates/creates (diff.go:303-316).

Outbound delete execution with durable intent/receipt already works for ordinary sync: Begin/RecordReceipt/Confirm (ee/integration/ledger/repository.go:87-146, 167-186, 240-257); Cloudflare Apply rereads the remote baseline, compares BeforeHash/IDs/versions, batches at most 200 effects with a cadence pause and records per-target facts (ee/integration/cloudflare/apply.go:54-152, 292-297, 349-364); a delete is Complete when no owned row remains (apply.go:255-259); host recovery confirms observed absence after an ambiguous attempt (ee/integration/host/engine.go:518-531).

Per-attempt request budget that survives rotation and failover: providerHost.Request charges a durable cluster-wide Cloudflare bucket of 1000 requests per 300 s before each HTTP attempt and re-fences after the charge (ee/integration/host/request.go:49-86; ee/integration/ledger/budget.go:29-99); mounted proof TestIntegrationRuntimeActualOutboundLedgerAndBudget (cmd/kudurru/integration_publish_test.go:62-120).

Per-instance elector and joined replacement (F09a, completion-plan.md:93): one elector key per namespace/name (ee/integration/host/lifecycle.go:40-42, 197-249), so a cleanup job reusing the same key is automatically exclusive with the normal job.

Exact-incarnation local ownership needed for an atomic purge: source-owned objects are identified by manager plus annotation derived from the full Owner including UID (cmd/kudurru/integration_source.go:25, 86-88; ee/integration/host/source.go:30-36) and the omission path already deletes only exact captured UID/RV objects in one command (integration_source.go:320-342).

Kubernetes RBAC already grants get/list/watch/create/patch/delete on `integrations` and update/patch on `integrations/status` (deploy/helm/kudurru/templates/rbac.yaml:14-18), which is enough to add and remove a finalizer by patch.

Only Cloudflare can own provider-side records in v0.2.0: UniFi pushes are refused (ee/integration/unifi/provider.go:224-229) and Tier-B webhook peers requiring records/hooks are refused (ee/integration/webhook/lifecycle.go:188), so provider cleanup scope is one adapter.

remaining.title: Store: reserved cleanup finalizer that survives whole-object Apply, plus a metadata-only finalizer write
remaining.detail: Today a manager's whole-object Apply replaces metadata.finalizers with whatever its document carries (internal/store/sqlite/crud.go:516-558) and, if the object is already terminating and the result is empty, finalizes it on the spot (crud.go:581-583). The file reconciler strips server metadata but not finalizers and ignores them when comparing (internal/objects/reconcile.go:496, 510-532), so an edited or re-declared Integration document would silently drop the cleanup obligation, i.e. Delete would degrade to Retain. Kubernetes server-side apply preserves another field manager's finalizer, except on the Force takeover path, which reassigns all field ownership and removes omitted fields (internal/store/kube/crud.go:158-160, 207-221). Required: (a) in internal/store/store.go define the reserved name `kudurru.io/integration-cleanup` and a pure rule 'for kind Integration the finalizer is present exactly when spec.deletionPolicy == Delete; a terminating object keeps it until the cleanup owner removes it or the spec is changed to Retain'; (b) apply that rule inside SQLite planApply after validation so it covers Store.Apply and CommandTx.Apply (internal/store/sqlite/command.go:366-390) atomically with the spec write (admission-time arming: no unarmed window and no extra resourceVersion churn); (c) in the kube driver carry the reserved finalizer through the Force/takeOver payload; (d) add an optional driver interface for a metadata-only finalizer mutation with exact UID and resourceVersion preconditions that preserves manager, spec, status and generation and finalizes a terminating object when the last finalizer is removed (SQLite: new CommandTx method next to Delete at command.go:392; Kubernetes: patch with optimistic lock under a distinct field manager). Replication installs images verbatim and needs no change (internal/store/sqlite/replication.go:205). Safe exports already strip finalizers and deletionTimestamp (cmd/kudurru/backup.go:91).
remaining.acceptance: Tracker: gaps.md:858-859 ('Delete needs a cleanup/finalizer protocol'); D239 rejected alternative 'silently treating Delete as Retain' (dev-docs/design-record.md:1839); D302 original delete identity (design-record.md:1909). Tests: extend internal/store/sqlite/sqlite_test.go TestFinalizers (:458) with (1) Apply of an Integration with Delete arms the finalizer in the same write, (2) same-manager Apply without finalizers, Apply with Force, and Apply during termination all keep it and do not finalize, (3) Apply switching to Retain on a live object disarms, and on a terminating object finalizes, (4) metadata-only removal with wrong UID or RV is ErrConflict and with correct ones emits Deleted. Mirror in internal/store/kube (envtest, next to crud_test.go:319) for non-Force SSA, Force takeover and the patch primitive. Add one shared case to internal/store/conformance/conformance.go. Extend cmd/kudurru/serving_object_sources_test.go:431 so removing an armed Integration document leaves a visible terminating object and re-adding the document does not finalize it.

remaining.title: Planner cleanup mode and ledger 'forget' transition
remaining.detail: Planner: add an explicit cleanup flag to plan.Input (ee/integration/plan/types.go:56-69) that requires an empty Desired set, forces PolicySync for owned keys instead of the per-zone or ledger-retained policy (today policyFor falls back to the retained policy for undesired keys, diff.go:108-118, and only PolicySync yields a delete, diff.go:218-221), and additionally requires ledger evidence for every provider ID it deletes (marker AND ledger ProviderIDs or the pending operation's IDs/receipt targets), so nothing is deleted on marker alone. The flag must be part of the plan digest (diff.go:283-293). Conflicted names stay untouched and are reported, exactly as today (diff.go:183-186). Cleanup intents carry Policy `sync`, which the Cloudflare adapter requires for a delete (ee/integration/cloudflare/apply.go:47). Ledger: add Repository.Forget for a row whose Pending is nil and whose baseline is confirmed absent (empty ContentHash and ProviderIDs after Confirm, repository.go:249-256), deleting the row and its terminal operations by exact resourceVersion; this needs a guarded Delete callback beside the existing Write in ledger.Options (ee/integration/ledger/types.go:44-59), wired on SQLite through the same fenced command as writes (cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go:473-487). Add a helper listing all ledger rows of an Owner across destinations (today ledgers() filters one destination, ee/integration/host/engine.go:286-329) so rows for destinations no longer in spec are detected and reported rather than ignored. IntegrationBudget rows must never be removed (D209: failover and rotation must not reset budgets, design-record.md:1809).
remaining.acceptance: Tracker: README.md:380 V2-INTEGRATIONS ('foreign/unowned records are protected ... retries are idempotent'); D206 ownership and durable receipts (design-record.md:1804). Tests: ee/integration/plan/plan_test.go: cleanup plan deletes only marker+ledger-proven rows; foreign-marker, unowned and external-dns-heritage rows untouched; a marker-owned row with no ledger evidence is reported, not deleted; upsert-only/create-only retained policy is overridden only in cleanup mode; reordered inputs give the same digest; capacity bounds hold. ee/integration/ledger/repository_test.go and sqlite_test.go: Forget refuses a pending row, a non-empty baseline, a stale RV and a stale guard; survives reopen; budget row untouched.

remaining.title: Host: elected, bounded terminating job
remaining.detail: Replace the `Paused/Deleting` branch (ee/integration/host/lifecycle.go:170-181) with a cleanup job when the captured definition is terminating, carries the reserved finalizer and has policy Delete; keep the existing cancel-and-join of the normal job first (lifecycle.go:111-118). The job reuses the same election key (lifecycle.go:40-42) and concurrency slot, takes a guard with an explicit cleanup mode on ExecutionGuard (ee/integration/host/types.go:38-42), then: Provision, Validate and Check with the captured named credentials as in runLease (commands.go:108-124) but without Start, observation or event delivery; for Publishers build publications with no sources (engine.go:22-107), run pending recovery first (engine.go:363-388), then execute cleanup-mode delete intents through the unchanged Begin, fence, Apply, RecordReceipt, Confirm sequence (engine.go:427-471); when a fresh complete reread shows no owned rows and no pending row, call Forget; then invoke new root callbacks for the atomic local purge and for finalization. Recovery needs one relaxation in cleanup mode only: a pending delete intent may be resumed even if the credential or config digest changed since it was recorded (today engine.go:541 requires equality), because authority comes from UID ownership plus the terminating guard, and recoveryDesired must evaluate with PolicySync (engine.go:589-601). Each run is bounded by OperationTimeout (types.go:248-250) and the request budget; runs repeat with the existing classified backoff (retry.go:34-53) until done. Blocking conditions never finalize: incomplete remote snapshot, a conflict at a name holding owned rows, an unresolved ambiguous receipt, ledger rows for a destination not in spec, credential error, suspended, license not allowed. Report phase `Terminating` with a specific reason and remaining counts through setLocal/publishStatus (lifecycle.go:312-324; commands.go:433-448). A terminating object whose policy is Retain is released with zero provider calls. Outbound jobs do not auto-retry a fence refusal (commands.go:226-237), so the cleanup loop must capture a fresh frame per run rather than hold one.
remaining.acceptance: Tracker: followup-audit.md:82 ('prove independent-instance lease loss/replacement; G09, G22') and :587 ('finish Delete/Kubernetes dependencies'); D209 (design-record.md:1809). Tests in ee/integration/host using engineFixture/fakePublisher (engine_test.go:80) and lifecycleFixture (lifecycle_test.go:38): terminating+finalizer+Delete elects, deletes, forgets and calls finalize exactly once; terminating+Retain calls finalize with zero provider calls; suspended, unlicensed and credential-error cases make no provider call and report distinct reasons; lease loss between Apply and receipt leaves a pending intent that the next lease resolves from a complete reread without a second mutation (pattern of engine_pending_recovery_test.go); conflict or incomplete snapshot blocks finalization; budget exhaustion makes no HTTP call and resumes in the next window with the budget row intact; same-name replacement cannot start until the cleanup job is joined.

remaining.title: SQLite root adapter: cleanup guards, atomic local purge, finalization, removal of the Delete refusal
remaining.detail: In cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go: remove the blanket refusal (lines 292-296) in the same change that lands the protocol; make fence (line 366) and integrationInputsCurrent (line 450) mode-aware: normal mode still requires a zero deletionTimestamp and, when policy is Delete, that the reserved finalizer is present in the transaction-read definition (so no intent or source commit can exist unarmed); cleanup mode requires same UID, non-zero deletionTimestamp, finalizer present and policy Delete, with the unchanged license, key, writer-token and publication pins (command(), lines 385-439). Skip terminating instances when deciding needsSources (lines 162-165). New callbacks registered in ih.Options (line 64-81): (1) local purge in ONE command transaction: delete source-owned DNSRecordSet/DNSZone objects by exact captured UID/RV using sourceOwned (cmd/kudurru/integration_source.go:86-88, same loop shape as 322-341), delete IntegrationSourceHead and its chunks, stage the global inventory with this source emptied (as commitSource does at 173-183), delete this Owner's IntegrationNameAllocation and IntegrationDelivery rows, then wait for publication to show the source root gone (awaitSource pattern, 345-367); (2) finalization in one transaction: verify no ledger, pending operation, source head/chunk, allocation or delivery row remains for the Owner, write an audit/log summary of deleted and retained counts, and remove the finalizer with the DEL-1 primitive, which deletes the object; (3) a release path for a terminating object whose policy became Retain that removes the finalizer with no provider I/O and is not gated on the integrations license (still requires the elected writer), so license expiry or a permanently lost credential cannot trap an object. stageIntegrationStatus (lines 540-557) writes Ready=False with reason Terminating/blocked reason and remaining counts while the object exists.

remaining.title: API and CLI: show terminating state, add a reviewed release command
remaining.detail: The trigger needs no new delete route: on SQLite an Integration can only arrive through file-declared objects, because `/objects` and `/apply` serve six kinds and reject the rest (internal/api/kinds.go:21-28; internal/api/objects.go:608-610), and removal is the file reconciler's orphan delete (internal/objects/reconcile.go:454-485), which already goes through finalizer-aware Delete. Required cases: (1) HappyPath: publish with Delete, assert the stored object already carries the finalizer at the first batch POST, seed a foreign-marker row, an unowned row and an external-dns-heritage pair, delete the Integration; expect a visible terminating object, then only owned IDs in delete batches, the three foreign/unowned rows byte-identical, zero ledger/operation rows for the Owner, budget row still present, Get returns not found, DNS answers unchanged, no credential bytes in the image. remaining.title: Kubernetes equivalent: finalizer on the Integration CR (blocked on the Kubernetes host mount)
remaining.detail: Nothing can be cleaned on Kubernetes today because no Integration executes there: serve.go:1083-1084 logs that background execution is unavailable and leaves integration administration nil, so the routes answer 503 (internal/api/integrations.go:153-155). The protocol is the same state machine with Kubernetes mechanics, and should land together with whichever change mounts an outbound publisher host on Kubernetes (the F09b 'Kubernetes atomic-source' dependency, completion-plan.md:94): (1) arming: there is no admission webhook, so the elected instance adds `kudurru.io/integration-cleanup` by patch with a resourceVersion precondition under its own field manager before Provision completes, and refuses to create any ledger intent until a fresh read shows it; (2) `kubectl delete` then yields deletionTimestamp from the apiserver (internal/store/kube/crud.go:267-273); (3) the cleanup job runs under the per-instance Lease elector with the Secret-resolved credential; provider deletes go through the same ledger sequence, whose writes are already single-object create-only or exact-RV CAS (ledger/repository.go:59, 73; budget.go:90), so two nodes cannot both reserve one record; a stale leader is additionally stopped by the adapter's remote reread before any effect (cloudflare/apply.go:54-87); (4) local purge is sequential exact-UID/RV deletes (D302), idempotent and resumable, not one transaction (same accepted model as D303/D365/D366); (5) finalizer removed last by patch with precondition; (6) manual finalizer removal or patching the policy to Retain is the documented escape and equals Retain. DEL-1 already covers keeping the finalizer through a Force takeover. RBAC needs no change (deploy/helm/kudurru/templates/rbac.yaml:14-18). If v0.2.0 ships with Kubernetes integration execution still disabled, this item reduces to the documentation statement in DEL-6 and must be recorded as not delivered on Kubernetes rather than closed.
remaining.acceptance: Tracker: gaps.md:858-859 ('Kubernetes needs a true atomic source/admission root, and Delete needs a cleanup/finalizer protocol; both remain explicit F09b work'), followup-audit.md:587. Envtest cases once a Kubernetes host exists (assets via `make envtest`, Makefile:91-94): finalizer present before the first provider write; delete leaves a terminating CR; cleanup deletes only owned provider records against the local HTTP double and removes private Secret-carried ledger rows; lease loss mid-cleanup hands over without a duplicate delete; Force apply by another manager keeps the finalizer; manual finalizer removal behaves as Retain; two-replica run in the style of the DNSEndpoint lease-loss acceptance (completion-plan.md:146).
dependsOn: Kubernetes integration host mount (F09b Kubernetes dependency, separate item)

recommendation:
Implement the SQLite lifecycle now (DEL-1 to DEL-7) with a reserved finalizer as the durable tombstone, and record it as one new decision; treat the Kubernetes half (DEL-8) as dependent on the separate Kubernetes host mount. There is no owner blocker: no hardware, credential or product decision is needed, and the accepted evidence form for Cloudflare is already the local verified-TLS double (gaps.md:2294; no live-account requirement exists in the tracker).

Protocol (both drivers, SQLite mechanics in parentheses):
1. Armed: an Integration with `deletionPolicy: Delete` always carries `kudurru.io/integration-cleanup` (SQLite sets it in the same write as the spec; every intent and source commit re-checks it in its transaction). No owned external state can exist unarmed.
2. Delete request: any deleter (file document removed, kubectl) hits the store's existing rule, so the object gets a deletionTimestamp in the delete transaction and stays readable with its spec, credential references, UID and status. This is the atomic tombstone; no new kind or delete API.
3. Quiesce: existing behavior cancels and joins the normal job and withdraws live inventory claims.
4. Cleanup run, elected on the same per-instance key, bounded per run and resumable: provision with the object's own credential reference; recover pending intents from a complete reread; plan deletes only for rows that carry this cluster+UID marker AND have ledger evidence; execute through the existing intent, fence, budgeted request, receipt, confirm path; forget ledger rows once absence is confirmed.
5. Local purge in one transaction: source-owned record sets and zones, source head and chunks, inventory contribution, name allocations, deliveries.
6. Finalize in one transaction: verify nothing remains for the Owner, write an audit summary, remove the finalizer.

Edge behavior to record:
- Credential missing: stay Terminating with a credentials reason, zero provider calls, resume when it returns. A rotated value of the same reference is accepted because ownership is proven by marker and ledger, and a token mapping to a different account produces a different destination and therefore blocks instead of deleting elsewhere.
- Restart and failover: all state is durable; a fenced writer cannot record or finalize; the successor resolves ambiguity by reread, never by blind replay.
- License expired or suspended: cleanup pauses with no provider I/O; release to Retain is local and not license-gated.
- Conflicts, uncertain receipts, or ledger rows for a destination no longer in spec: block and report; never finish partially in silence.
- The shared request budget row is never deleted.

Sub-decisions I would make and log: (a) `Delete` overrides per-zone `upsert-only`/`create-only` for proven-owned records, because the research note defines it as the separate knob 'for when the sink itself is removed' (dev-docs/research/integrations.md:472-473); the conservative alternative (honor the retained policy) is a one-line planner difference. (b) Arm at admission on SQLite and by the host on Kubernetes.

Precedents followed: D197 (Retain default, references only), D206 (ownership is cluster+UID with ledger evidence; baseline advances only on confirmed receipts), D209 (per-attempt budgets, recovery from complete rereads, no reset on failover), D239 (never silently treat Delete as Retain), D291 (reviewed commands bind UID and revision), D302 (delete with original UID/RV identity), D303/D365/D366 (Kubernetes designs built on single-object CAS and convergence rather than a fabricated transaction).

Order: DEL-1 and DEL-2 in parallel, then DEL-3, DEL-4, then DEL-5/DEL-6/DEL-7. The refusal at integration_runtime.go:292-296 must be removed only in the change that lands DEL-4, otherwise Delete becomes a silent Retain. If the release cannot absorb this, the fallback is to keep the refusal and only improve its status reason, but that leaves F09b open and is a scope call for the owner rather than an engineering necessity.

designOptions.name: A. Reserved finalizer on the Integration object (recommended)
designOptions.description: `kudurru.io/integration-cleanup` is present whenever policy is Delete. The store's existing delete-with-finalizer rule provides the terminating state; an elected cleanup job deletes ledger-proven provider records, purges local state atomically and removes the finalizer. Same model on SQLite and Kubernetes.
designOptions.pros: No new durable kind, format version or replication manifest change. Finalizer semantics already exist and are tested in both drivers (sqlite crud.go:581-583, 603-666; kube crud.go:267-273). The object keeps spec, credential references, UID and a status surface while terminating. Works for every delete path, including file-document removal, which is the only SQLite path today. Host and root already model the deleting state (lifecycle.go:170-181; integration_runtime.go:366, 450). kubectl-native on Kubernetes.
designOptions.cons: Requires store hardening so a whole-object Apply or Force takeover cannot strip the finalizer (sqlite crud.go:516-558; kube crud.go:158-160) and a metadata-only finalizer write. A terminating object holds its name, so same-name re-declaration edits the old object until cleanup finishes. A stuck cleanup needs an explicit release path.

designOptions.name: B. Private tombstone kind written ahead of deletion
designOptions.description: A new private runtime kind captures Owner, policy, credential references and provider settings when the instance is armed; the public object is deleted immediately and the host cleans up from the tombstone plus ledger.
designOptions.pros: Public delete is immediate and the name is free at once. Immune to whole-object Apply. No change to store Apply semantics.
designOptions.cons: New private kind must be registered in every carrier, backup and replication manifest (api/integrationkinds/v1alpha1/types.go:27-29) and versioned. It must track every spec and credential-reference change atomically with the first effect, which Kubernetes cannot do. No public status once the object is gone. A recreated same-name object shares the election key with the old UID's cleanup. Stores credential references in a second place (D197 scrutiny). The two drivers diverge.

designOptions.name: C. Synchronous cleanup inside an explicit reviewed delete command
designOptions.description: A new `integrations delete` operation previews the cleanup plan, executes provider deletes under the reviewed-operation machinery (D291) and deletes the object in its final transaction.
designOptions.pros: Operator reviews the exact delete plan first. Reuses the existing operation proof and uncertainty reporting (cmd/kudurru/integration_operation.go).
designOptions.cons: Does not cover file-document removal or kubectl delete, which are the real deletion paths (internal/api/kinds.go:21-28; objects.go:608-610). The 30-second operation bound (integration_operation.go:76) cannot fit large zones under a 1000-requests-per-300-seconds budget and one-second batch cadence. A crash or failover mid-run still needs a durable terminating state, which collapses into option A. Reasonable later as a preview on top of A.

designOptions.name: D. Keep refusing Delete in v0.2.0
designOptions.description: Leave integration_runtime.go:292-296 in place, improve the status reason from ProvisionFailed to an explicit unsupported-policy reason, and document the limitation.
designOptions.pros: Zero new risk; already implemented, tested and documented.
designOptions.cons: F09b stays open against gaps.md:859 and followup-audit.md:587. The public schema keeps advertising a value that disables the instance. Retain leaves records a recreated Integration cannot adopt (ownership.go:34-37), so operators have no supported way to remove what an integration published. Descoping would be an owner decision.

risks: Finalizer stripping turns Delete into a silent Retain: SQLite whole-object Apply takes finalizers from the caller's document and finalizes a terminating object when none remain (internal/store/sqlite/crud.go:516-558, 581-583); the file reconciler does not sanitize or compare finalizers (internal/objects/reconcile.go:496, 510-532); Kubernetes Force takeover removes fields the new manager omits (internal/store/kube/crud.go:158-160). DEL-1 must land first.

Removing the refusal at cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go:292-296 before the full protocol exists would make Delete behave as Retain, the exact outcome D239 rejects. Land it atomically with DEL-4 and rewrite the test at integration_runtime_test.go:345.

On SQLite there is no API, CLI or UI path to create, edit or delete an Integration: `/objects` and `/apply` only serve six kinds (internal/api/kinds.go:21-28; internal/api/objects.go:608-610). Deletion means removing the document from the objects file, and 'edit the terminating object' means re-declaring it, which is awkward; the release command is the practical escape. Whether Integration should join the generic object routes is a separate tracker concern (README.md:403).

Ledger rows for a destination that was removed from spec before the Integration was deleted are never planned, because publications come only from configured zones (ee/integration/host/engine.go:22-97; cloudflare/provider.go:219-300). Cleanup must detect and block on them. The same gap already orphans remote records during ordinary sync when a zone is removed from spec.

Cleanup can take a long time and competes for a shared budget: 10,000 records per zone cap (cloudflare/provider.go:32; plan/diff.go:41-46), 200 effects per batch with a one-second cadence (apply.go:95, 349-364), 1000 requests per 300 s for all Cloudflare instances in the cluster (host/request.go:71-75), 30 s default operation timeout (host/types.go:248-250). It must be resumable across runs, and other publishers will slow down while a large cleanup runs.

Outbound jobs do not automatically retry after a fence refusal (ee/integration/host/commands.go:226-237). Any design that changes the object's resourceVersion inside a lease (for example host-side arming on Kubernetes) can stall the first publication until the next resync unless the job re-captures its frame first.

Recovery rules are stricter than cleanup needs: resuming a partially applied intent requires unchanged config and credential digests (engine.go:541) and Abandon refuses any applied target (ledger/repository.go:273-277). Without the cleanup-mode relaxation in DEL-3, a credential rotation between a partial delete and its recovery leaves the object Terminating forever.

License expiry or a permanently lost credential traps a Delete-policy object in Terminating unless the release path exists and is not gated on the integrations license (host gating at cmd/kudurru/integration_runtime.go:64-67; lifecycle.go:111, 170-174).

A terminating object keeps its name in both drivers, so a same-name re-apply modifies the old incarnation instead of creating a new one, and the new incarnation cannot start until cleanup finishes. Operators deleting and immediately recreating will see a delay.

Under Retain, a recreated Integration has a new UID and sees the previous incarnation's records as a foreign marker that explicit adoption cannot take over (cloudflare/ownership.go:34-37; host/engine.go:263-268), so they become permanent conflicts. This is existing behavior that the docs do not state and that makes Delete more important than the tracker wording suggests.

Private rows are never garbage collected today: no non-test code deletes IntegrationLedger or IntegrationOperation rows, and name allocations are permanent and counted against a cluster cap (ee/integration/inbound/image.go:257). Cleanup must remove terminal operations for the Owner, and Retain will keep leaking rows; docs/architecture/integrations.md:143-144 already flags retention cleanup for deliveries.

After finalization the object and its status are gone, so the cleanup outcome (deleted, retained, blocked-then-released counts) must be written to the audit log or structured log before the finalizer is removed, or there is no record of what was deleted.

Kubernetes: the host is not mounted (cmd/kudurru/serve.go:1083-1084), so the Kubernetes protocol cannot be exercised or evidenced until that separate work lands. If v0.2.0 ships without it, the CRD still accepts `Delete` on Kubernetes with no effect and the docs must say so explicitly; the item cannot be recorded as closed on both drivers.

The policy-override choice (Delete versus per-zone upsert-only/create-only) changes what gets deleted for existing configurations. It is an engineering decision to log, but the operator guide must state it plainly, and the Cloudflare adapter rejects a delete intent that carries an upsert-only policy (cloudflare/apply.go:47), so the planner and adapter must agree.

Mounted tests live in the slow, crowded `package main` under cmd/kudurru with shared fixtures; parallel work on integration tests there is a likely merge-conflict and runtime-budget hot spot (gaps.md:2895-2899).
